Moving on: When the righteous men rejoice, there is great glory. When God has blessed His people with leaders who openly praise His name, we have the opportunity for glory. But when the wicked men rise, the righteous are hidden.

Tying this again to soul-winning, evangelizing to the lost, praising God's name in the open, or even reading the Bible and speaking His word confidently, is easy in modern America, today. We have the freedom to openly glorify God. Our leaders, even if they are wolves and deceivers, pay lip service to the Lord and believers are able to openly proclaim Christ without fear.

Yet so many men are hidden, still. It's a shame that many churches do not have any soul-winning. That many Christians hide who they are, and what Jesus has done for them. That so few read the Bible here, while there are countries where reading scripture can be a prison sentence. That confessing Christ can end in death.

Maybe it is a parallel to the rich young man. That by our comfort and safety we grow complacent. Maybe revival requires tribulation. Maybe the embarrassment of riches we have in the freedom we've been granted by God has caused too many Christians to have their heart hardened for the lost.

Vs 13; *He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.*

We know that in Christ our sins are forgiven, past, present and future. But we are also to faithfully confess our sins to the Father, Who is faithful again to forgive.

Covering sin leads to the chastening of the Lord. Humbling ourselves to admit our failings will have mercy.

Keeping the theme going, you can see how those Christians who don't go to church, don't read their Bible, don't spread the gospel, would rather hide their sin than acknowledge and forsake them. If they confess, they're conceding to God that they know better, and if they agree that His way is the way forward, then they cannot continue on in theirs.

They become paralyzed by their own guilty conscience and love of their sin.

"If I go to church, I am admitting I should, and so now I am on the hook to keep going." Same with Bible reading, prayer, or evangelizing.

We read in vs 9 that if you hate hearing the law because you want to continue doing the things God says you shouldn't, even your prayers shall be abominations.

How much worse are our prayers when we have the liberty to go to church, to get plugged in, to hear hard preaching, to learn God's word, to hear the law and confess our sins and be forgiven, and have the freedom to joyfully tell others the riches of God, and yet we ignore it all?

Is it any wonder we end up with a wicked ruler will rise up over a spiritually poor people? To take away the things and riches we take for granted? To provoke God's people to turn again to Him and do what's right, that He may heal the land?

V 14-15 seem to be separate points, yet in this larger context they reveal a greater truth;

*Happy is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief. As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.*

Don't harden your hearts. Humble yourself. Confess your sins, including those that come from omissions. To know to do good and to do it not. Return to the first love. Obey the Great Commission. We have been given the ministry of reconciliation, and the opportunity to be servants to the Lord. Don't squander it. Redeem the time. Repent, ask forgiveness and turn to the paths of the Lord.

teachings.title: Calling upon the name of the Lord
teachings.summary: Says calling on the Lord is admitting you are a sinner and confessing He is the Christ, not turning from sins, asking Jesus into your heart or giving your life to Him.
teachings.text:
Admitting that you're a sinner. Not "turning from your sins.

Calling upon the name of the Lord isn't "asking Jesus into your heart." It's confessing He is the Christ.

It's not giving your life to Jesus, it's knowing He gave His for you.

teachings.title: St. Patrick, an independent missionary
teachings.summary: Quotes Patrick's Confessio to show a 5th century missionary preaching grace by faith and soul winning, outside papal authority.
teachings.text:
St. Patrick was a Baptist missionary sent to Ireland by the independent church in Britain, to preach the gospel, which in Confessio 4, he quotes:

"...He poured out his Holy Spirit on us in abundance, the gift and pledge of immortality, which makes the believers and the obedient into sons of God and co-heirs of Christ who is revealed... Let every tongue confess that Jesus Christ, in whom we believe and whom we await to come back to us... is Lord and God. He is judge of the living and of the dead; he rewards every person according to their deeds."

Confessio 14–15:
"In the knowledge of this faith in the Trinity... it is right to make known the gift of God and his eternal consolation... I didn’t deserve at all that the Lord would grant such great grace, after hardships and troubles, after captivity, and after so many years among that people."

Patrick affirms that obedience to the gospel, and receiving the gift of eternal life and sonship, being co-heirs with Christ, is by the grace of God, and received by faith.

Confessio 3:
"Hence I cannot be silent... about the great benefits and the great grace which the Lord has deigned to bestow upon me in the land of my captivity... for this we can give to God in return after having been chastened by Him, to exalt and praise His wonders."

It's worth noting that while Patrick lived shortly after Augustine and Pelagius, his isolation from them and Rome and their introduction of determinism heresy that became Calvinism, he was notably silent on the matter of free will. Preaching a pure Gospel of grace received by faith.

Confessio 38:
"I am very much God's debtor, who gave me such grace that many people were reborn in God through me and afterwards confirmed... for a people just coming to the faith, whom the Lord took from the utmost parts of the earth."

Patrick, saw the new birth (eternal life/regeneration) as coming by grace to those "coming to the faith"—faith as the response to the gospel call.

In Confessio 12, Patrick echoes the same amazement at the grace of God, that saves a wretch like me and you and him.

"Before I was brought low, I was like a stone lying deep in the mud. Then he who is powerful came and in his mercy pulled me out, and lifted me up... That is why I must shout aloud in return to the Lord for such great good deeds of his... which the human mind cannot measure."

In Confessio 33, Brother Patrick wrote on his soul-winning mission:

"The Spirit was fervent within me... I pray to God to give me perseverance and to deign that I be a faithful witness to Him to the end of my life for my God."

It is the same drive we should strive for today. Patrick was a great soul winner. We should emulate him, and his passion for the gospel, rather than the drunken revelry and excess that Catholics despoil his legacy with. Green beer and bawdy behavior Is more fitting with the pagans he brought the gospel to than those professing Christ.

It was this love of God and the people of Ireland, that gave him innumerable souls won to the Lord.

Confessio 41 (on the Irish converts):
"How has it lately come about in Ireland that those who never had any knowledge of God... have now been made a people of the Lord, and are called sons of God... How many have been reborn there so as to be of our kind, I do not know..."

Patrick's great success in winning people to Christ is why reclaiming his legacy from the Catholics matters. To be an inspiration to us today. That we don't faint in adversity or fall into the snares of the world.

Confessio 16:
"The love of God and His fear came to me more and more, and my faith was strengthened. Faith grew, and my spirit was moved..."

Patrick's doctrine shines through his writings; eternal life is by grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone.

Stripping away the invented Catholic hagiography of St. Patrick to reveal the tremendous man of faith behind their legend also reveals that independent churches existed in the 4th and 5th century, with tenuous or no ties to Rome or papal authority. And that their understanding of the Gospel was the same biblical understanding used by Baptists today.

Patrick, as an evangelical figure from a non-Roman British church tradition, independent of papal authority, does away with the common tropes and traditions Catholics claim always existed in the church.

He relies on Scripture alone, emphasizing a believer's response to the gospel, and avoids entirely Catholic elements like intercession of saints, Mary, purgatory, falling out of Grace, priestly confession, veneration of images and idols... All are absent from his writings which are entirely gospel focused.

His Confessio shows no appeal to Rome for legitimacy, but a strong focus on personal faith and grace, and his mission as the first documented major "independent" missionary enterprise, post-apostles.

The most reputable biographies show that Patrick was British (born ~late 4th/early 5th century), enslaved in Ireland as a youth, escaped, then trained/ordained in Britain (likely as deacon/priest then bishop, possibly in the church his father and grandfather served as elders), and returned as a missionary around 432 AD. A third generation Christian, who potentially could trace by his patriarchal lineage, a direct line to first century Christianity.

He describes his authority as being given by a divinely called mission, he appeals to no pope or hierarchy for validation, and his Confessio defends his mission against British critics who questioned his calling to Ireland and his burden for the same people who had enslaved him.

Patrick does not describe or mention baby/infant baptism (paedobaptism) at any point in his writings.

The two surviving documents universally accepted as genuinely from Patrick himself—his Confessio (Confession) and the Letter to the Soldiers of Coroticus (Epistola), contain several references to baptism, but all of them describe baptisms of converted believers, adults or those who have come to faith through hearing the Gospel, and confession of their faith.

Patrick emphasizes baptism in the context of missionary preaching: teaching first, then baptizing those who believe, aligning with the Great Commission, which he quotes repeatedly in his writings. All water baptisms Patrick mentions are of converted believers who confirm their faith through response to the Gospel. No babies or infants are referenced.

The true gospel of eternal life and believer's baptism are all he knew, and all he related to others.

teachings.title: Deliver them that are drawn unto death
teachings.summary: Every man is judged by his works, believers at the bema seat for reward and the lost at the Great White Throne, so a believer who fails to give the gospel to the perishing cannot plead ignorance and will suffer loss.
teachings.text:
Continuing the fatherly advice of the King, Solomon, to his son the prince, **Proverbs 24:11-12**;

*If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain; If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?*

He says that failure to deliver someone marked for death by claiming ignorance to the circumstances, and potentially the injustice or false accusations that led to it, by not hearing the matter fully - that it is not an excuse. Solomon writes that we should consider our own soul, the Lord's mercy upon it, His judgment. That He will judge every man according to his works.

This is echoed in the New Testament.

**Romans 2:4-9**
*Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; Who will render to every man according to his deeds: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile*

**Hebrews 9:27**
*And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.*

The wages of sin is death. We are all guilty. We will all be judged. But those in faith, who have believed on Christ, our sins not being imputed against our record, being justified by the righteousness of Jesus, our works, being built upon that foundation, are judged at the bema seat of Christ, to see what sort of works they are.

**1 Corinthians 3:12-15**
*Now if any man build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble; Every man's work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is. If any man's work abide which he hath built thereupon, he shall receive a reward. If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.*

We are still saved, but, based on the criteria of God; the good will be rewarded and the vain and meaningless, destroyed.

Meanwhile, the unbelieving are judged by their works at the Great White Throne. Their works held against them;

**Revelation 20:11-15**
*And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.*

With this perspective, which Solomon clearly understood, a ruler must make the effort to know what he is judging, especially in a capital crime where a life hangs in jeopardy.

This warning applies to those that are princes by faith, in the Kingdom of God. To believers, every man we meet is appointed to death and Hell for their sins. They are drawn unto death, and ready to be slain.

If we forbear to deliver them, to give them the gospel, we cannot say we didn't know. He that pondereth the heart and keepeth our soul, He knows it. And it will be counted a loss in the trying fire at the judgment seat of Christ.

teachings.title: Cast not your pearls before swine
teachings.summary: Fools despise wisdom, so whether online or soul winning door to door we should give our piece, reject the heretic after admonition, shake off the dust and not be trapped in debate.
teachings.text:
Next, we are told to not speak wisdom to the fool, for they despise it. They do not value wise words, or that which is holy;

**Matthew 7:6**
*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.*

Jesus' words against giving the word of God to dogs and swine, the sodomites and the reprobate, is an escalation to the proverb. Just as we will see, arguing with fools and the wicked is vanity in later chapters. It is important to keep in mind, especially today with the Internet culture, where endless debate and the need to prove someone is "wrong on the Internet" can become a hazard. A snare I struggle with.

**Titus 3:10**
*A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject.*..

As Jesus instructs the Apostles, shake the dust. When we are out soul-winning, going door to door with the gospel, never get into arguments with the unreceptive or the mockers or blasphemers. You simply let them oppose themselves and move on.

Remembering that the foolish despise wisdom is a great way to train yourself to not be trapped in debate, but to say your piece and move on. Their own blood is on their own head. Wash your hands of it.

teachings.title: The wise son and the diligent hand
teachings.summary: Proverbs contrasts the diligent, righteous and wise with the lazy fool; God provides for those who work, and the wise gather the harvest, including winning souls.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 10** begins the more familiar listing of wise sayings, made in the Spirit by Solomon, his proverbs. But the lesson contrasting the righteous listening to instruction, being industrious, refraining from speaking evil and being wise, with the fool who is lazy, full of iniquity and violence, with a froward mouth, continues to be the primary theme carried over from the introduction in chapters 1-9.

Verse 1 contains an eternal truth that any parent could attest to. Establishing early the wisdom to found is accurate and true. A wise son is the pride of a dad, while the foolish son is the heaviness and sorrow of his mother.

From this base, the sayings stack up, precept upon precept, truth on truth. Building a foundation of wisdom that, sadly is lacking in the world today, because most, even many Christians, don't harken to the word of God. They do not fear Him, and so do not have His wisdom to rely on. They do not acknowledge Him in all their ways, and so He isn't there to direct their paths.

There are also proverbs given that have become ingrained in the secular lexicon (even if they don't acknowledge it). Such as the first half of verse 2; Gain made by wicked deeds profit nothing. In other words, crime doesn't pay. But the wise counter to this truth is that the way of the righteous delivers one from death.

We are told the truth of the Lord that He will provide for His own, the righteous won't famish, while He destroys the substance of the wicked. Not a prosperity gospel, but the understanding that when you walk in the Spirit, working in righteousness, the Lord will take care of your basic needs.

**Luke 12:27-31**
*Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith? And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind. For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things. But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

This is a promise of Christ Jesus Himself, with the caveat that the poor often are that way by being slackers, not diligent in their works.

**2 Thessalonians 3:10**
*For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.*

God blesses those that prepare, gathering in the summer against the winter is wise. Sleeping through the harvest is a shame. Being forward thinking and considering the end of something, understanding consequences, cause and effect, is wisdom. Shortsighted sin leads to shame.

Of course, the harvest analogy is not just applicable to agrarian cultures, or to earthly financial goals, but also the sharing of the gospel of Christ's Kingdom is frequently likened to the harvest.

**John 4:35**
*Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.*

Go soul-winning! The workers are few and the harvest is plenty. He that winneth souls is wise.

**Psalm 126:6**
*He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.*

But the sluggard who buries his talent of silver, to mix metaphors, he will be ashamed. He will not have sheaves of glory to rejoice in.

Being a just man, fair and merciful, extending grace to others, brings blessings and glory. The Lord will esteem the name of the just but the fool will die unknown, they will fall.

Walk upright, consider what you say. Don't be a prattling fool or a subtle and froward man, or a man of violence and offense, stirring up strifes and hatred. Knowing love covereth all sins.

**1 Peter 4:8**
*And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins.*

teachings.title: Reprove not a scorner; shake off the dust
teachings.summary: As Christ and Paul taught, we do not argue with scorners when giving the gospel but shake off the dust and move on, while instruction to the wise makes them wiser, each man bearing his own guilt.
teachings.text:
Solomon then gives this instruction; *Forsake the foolish, and live.* He says to not reprove a scorner, to not rebuke the wicked. This is echoed in the way Christ gave to His disciples when sending them out to the lost sheep of Israel;

**Mathew 10:14** *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet*.

As Paul instructs Titus;

**Titus 3:10** *A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject*

These men oppose themselves.

Peter writes that we should not argue with scoffers; *Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing*.

**1 Peter 3:16** *Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

When we are out in the hedges and highways, compelling all to come to the wisdom of God, by His gospel, we aren't there to argue. To debate. We are not supposed to waste our time with scoffers and mockers and scorners of the truth. We are supposed to shake the dust and move on.

But, if we give instruction to the wise, they will be wiser. Those seeking the truth will hear us. They will understand that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

And by His wisdom, our days are lengthened, our life increased.

It is on every man to bear this. To the wise, for themselves and to life; for the scorner, to themselves unto death.

This is individual soul liberty. We carry our own guilt and are responsible. But by faith we enter into His grace.

teachings.title: Peter's denial and ours
teachings.summary: Uses Luke 22:62, Galatians 2:11-14 and 2 Peter 2 to show that even mature believers can deny Christ under social pressure, yet Peter went on to preach boldly.
teachings.text:
**Luke 22:62**
*And Peter went out, and wept bitterly. *

There are times in every Christian's life where the story of Peter's betrayal of Christ hits hard. New Christians, who have just accepted the gospel and been saved, turn to their unsaved family and friends, and at the slightest pushback and mocking, get embarrassed and deny Jesus.

Older, more mature Christians even, will keep their faith hidden in social settings or in the workplace.

We may miss opportunities to go soul winning with our brothers and sisters, in part because of the fear of judgment. That you will be accused by scoffers as Peter was, and so preemptively decline to go.

We all have a regret of not sharing the gospel in a time and place where we are given the opportunity by God to proclaim the faith that saved us.

We may weep bitterly by the hospital bed of someone close to us, incapable of knowing the truth because we never shared it.

The Apostle Peter's story in the gospels is very real and relatable. But it doesn't end at the crowing of the cock that morning.

The risen Christ appears to Peter again during the 40 days between Easter and the Ascension. Peter, unsure of his calling and, I think, ashamed of his betrayal before the Son of God, decided to go fishing.

**John 21:1-4**
*After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself. There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples. Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.*

And as Jesus prepares them food, and eats with them, He gives Peter, who denied Him 3 times, the opportunity to affirm his love of Jesus 3 times.

**John 21:14-17**
*This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep. He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. *

Peter always loved Jesus, and trusted Him, but his shame for the denial of his Lord in His hour of death made him feel distant and alone. Jesus gave him the opportunity to work through that shame and realize his love for Christ is greater than his shame at letting Jesus down.

And Jesus says at each affirmation, *feed My sheep*. Serve others. Win souls. Care for the flock.

The answer to the shame we feel when we deny Christ or the opportunity to share Him with others, isn't to go fishing. To return to the world. But to return to the work of the ministry of reconciliation we all have.

Soul-winning when you are down bad, and ashamed, when prayer feels a little empty, when Bible reading is falling off, when you know you gotta get right, even if you aren't backsliding, per se, is the way to show yourself the love of Jesus you have. It is restorative sharing with others the love He has for you, and them.

Peter's story doesn't end there, either. In Acts we see him boldly proclaiming Christ, calling Jews to repentance and faith towards God. Enduring beatings and imprisonment to preach the gospel. Of going to the Gentiles with the truth when called by God.

And even then, Peter isn't perfect. Even as an elder of the faith, he still occasionally felt the pressure to conform to the world. Here, he is called out by Paul.

**Galatians 2:11-14**
*But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?*

It is something we can all fall into, even as older more mature Christians.

That's why, when Peter writes his epistles, his encouraging message to believers to hold fast their faith, even when facing scoffers, mockers, false teachers, etc...to be like Christ when we are reviled for His sake - is so powerful. Like most good preaching, he is talking about his own struggles, to edify others.

**1 Peter 2:21-23**
 *For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth: Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously*

Being ready to testify of the hope we have even as men falsely accused us, mocking and scoffing our faith, to have the mind of Christ:

**1 Peter 3:13-16** 
*And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good? But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled; But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.*

Even as Noah suffered the scoffers and blasphemers of the pre-flood world, as he prepared the ark, those spirits in Hell that Jesus went and preached to, showing those that trust the Lord shall not be ashamed;

Those *spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water. *

Peter says the flood that destroyed those wicked people is a like figure to the baptism of the believer, showing the same faith and confidence Noah had to build the ark, saving his family.

*The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.*..

Our obedience in baptism, to publicly proclaim our faith, similarly shuts the mouths of those scoffers, that our conscience is clean in Christ.

 **2 Peter 2:1-3**
*But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction. And many shall follow their pernicious ways; by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of And through covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose judgment now of a long time lingereth not, and their damnation slumbereth not.*

Verse 7-8, *how God delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

Speaking of a believer who didn't share his faith, just Lot still was delivered from their filthy conversation, just as God promises to deliver us from the same mockers and unrighteous people.

*cursed children: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet.*

**2 Peter 3:3**
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts.*..


And so let's learn from Peter's slip ups and mistakes, and take heart in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

**2 Peter 3:17-18**
*Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.*

I think many of us like to think of ourselves as Paul, but if we are honest, we are a lot more like Peter.

teachings.title: Win souls until the day of Christ
teachings.summary: Quotes 2 Thessalonians 2 to show the falling away and the man of sin come first, so believers should win souls until then.
teachings.text:
*Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him, That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God. Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?

And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time. For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way. And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming*

The imminent return of Christ is true...after all these things come to pass. Until they do, win souls!

teachings.title: The parable of the sower
teachings.summary: Notes that in Matthew 13 the wayside hearers are unsaved while the other three receive the word, though only the last bring forth fruit.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 13:18-23 **
*Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower. When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.

But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is **he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it**; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.

He also that **received seed** among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and **he becometh unfruitful**.

But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; **which also beareth fruit, **and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.*

Note that in the parable of the sower, the first group are unsaved, those of the wayside.

The other 3 are saved, receiving the word, but for the reasons given, the 2nd and 3rd aren't fruitful or become unfruitful. Yet they still are saved. The 4th are successful Christians, fruitful in bringing forth more believers, winning souls.

There is no example of someone who receives the seed, then becomes the hardpan ground of the wayside, no longer believing, and then sprouting and growing roots yet again

teachings.title: Living waters flowing out from Jerusalem
teachings.summary: The river from Ezekiel's temple pictures the Spirit and the gospel flowing out from Jerusalem, with believers as fruitful trees by the river as in Psalm 1 and John 7.
teachings.text:
Here in the penultimate chapter of Ezekiel, continuing with the prophecy of the Temple, we find the prophet brought out with the man guiding him before, who had the measure in his hands, and observing the flowing of water out of the altar and beyond the Temple and the courtyard.

And the further they went, the deeper the water became, from his ankle to his knees, to his loins. Eventually, to a mighty river that could not be passed over, deep enough to swim in.

Returning to the river's brink, the shore along a steep rise, and there he observed the trees on both sides. The angels tells him that the waters themselves that issue out of the Temple will eventually fill the desert, and the seas, healing all they touch, everything *shall live whither the river cometh*.

Living waters emanating from Jerusalem, trees lining their banks.

In **Psalm 1**, the Bible says we who delight in the Lord and His word are like unto trees planted by a river, that brings forth fruit, and the leaves shall not whither.

The prophet Zachariah preaches that in the day of the Lord, among the other things that occur, would be Jesus splitting the mount of Olives in Jerusalem, and in that day *living waters* shall go out from Jerusalem.

In the gospel of John, Jesus says that out of the belly of believers shall flow rivers of living water, and that this was a picture of the Spirit which they that believe on Him should receive.

Later, in the Revelation of Jesus given John, the new Heaven and heavenly Jerusalem has a river, and the tree of life upon it, which gives 12 different fruits every month, and whose leaves were for healing the nations.

The natural application for the initial prophecy given Ezekiel is a restored kingdom, with a river of waters healing the land, trees grown up from its shores, and full of all types of fish in abundance.

But spiritually, this is fulfilled in the ministry of Christ, and the spreading of the Gospel, as living waters, the Spirit, and wherever it went, healing the nations, and believers being as trees bearing fruit, other believers, springing up alongside the brink.

Prophetically, this matches the pattern in the end times shown John, of New Jerusalem.

If you are like the righteous man in **Psalm 1**, the believer in **John 7**, you are a tree bearing fruit, and from you flows the Spirit, living waters, His word.

Notice, the river begins in Jerusalem and gets deeper and deeper the further it travels.

And note too, that there are miry places, salt marshes that shall not be healed.

That the Mt Olive prophecy in Zachariah talks about the split, and a war between Judah.

There are those who will not receive the truth. There were Jews who would not believe, and they killed Christ and persecuted His followers.

teachings.title: Hope for the dead and the true gospel
teachings.summary: Says many have a false hope that anyone who acknowledged God was saved, and that the answer is soul winning and preaching the whole word to the living.
teachings.text:
Between the Pope, John MacArthur and Ozzy dying, it's really exposed how vacant and lost most people's understanding of salvation is.

People believe all manner of nonsense and vain beliefs, the primary one being that if someone vaguely acknowledged God in some way, or mentioned Jesus, that they were likely saved.

Of course the same people promoting this desperate false hope will turn to the living and say "You can't just say a prayer and be saved!" Mock "easy believism," and "once saved, always saved."

"You can't be saved and live however you want!"

"We are saved by faith....BUT...."

They will promote false teachers and men who profess another gospel, or worse, unregenerate celebrities who outright tell you they believe some unbiblical nonsense about "a higher power," and get angry when we point to scripture and the specific plan of salvation given to show that we can pretty much guarantee these people died in their sins and went to Hell.

"Only God can judge! You don't know what's in their hearts!"

God told us His judgement, and out of the abundance of their hearts, they spoke. We don't condemn them, their own words do.

**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

"Maybe God will be merciful to them!" He was when He sent His only begotten Son to die for us.

"Maybe they repented on their death bed!" Maybe, but if they didn't hear Moses and the prophets and the gospels and the preachers their whole life, they probably won't.

This is why we go soul-winning. This is why we preach the whole word, in season and out.

Hopes and prayers that someone gets right at the last moment, or wishing someone be saved after they die, are all vanity.

There is the gospel, preached by the saved to the lost, and the Spirit moving with their spirit, that they repent towards the gospel of grace and reconciliation in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: When Paul was saved
teachings.summary: Says Paul was not saved on the road to Damascus but in Damascus when he called on the Lord after Ananias taught him the gospel, and that no one is saved without hearing the word preached.
teachings.text:
I've heard many dispensationalists claim that the 144,000 of the book of Revelation are actually modern Jews, who unbeknownst to them carry the exact genetics of the 12 tribes mentioned, and they are given salvation in some sort of Calvinist way "Similar to Paul on the road to Damascus."

Paul did not get saved when he was blinded and heard the voice of Christ. Paul was saved in Damascus 3 days later when he called upon the name of the Lord after being instructed in the gospel by Ananias.

Every saved person has another saved person who acted as their minister of the Gospel of reconciliation to bring them to Christ. Nobody is given salvation without hearing the word preached and believing what they heard.

teachings.title: The gospel is not a call to discipleship
teachings.summary: Says the gospel Jesus proclaimed is repentance unto belief and calling on the Lord for eternal life by His blood, not a requirement of submissive obedience.
teachings.text:
This is not the gospel that Jesus proclaimed. It is a decision, repentance unto belief. A prayer, calling upon the name of the Lord. It was not a "call to discipleship" or a requirement for "submissive obedience."

It is eternal life and forgiveness of sins by the blood of Christ Jesus, because we aren't capable of submissive obedience or sufficient discipleship to ever pay any of the wages of sin. Our filthy rags aren't what the Lord wants. Faith is.

John MacArthur's heresy is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: The law as schoolmaster
teachings.summary: Asks how there can be revival without the law, since the law is the schoolmaster that brings the lost to repentance toward the gospel.
teachings.text:
How can there be revival without the law, when the law is the schoolmaster that brings the lost to repentance towards the gospel?

The haters of the law and hard preaching against sin essentially want to take away the schoolmaster. How can someone know they are wrong if they don't know what's right?

teachings.title: The remnant are not chosen but seek Him
teachings.summary: The remnant in Amos 5 is not a Calvinist election of certain men but the promise that whoever seeks the Lord shall live.
teachings.text:
**Amos 5** continues the prophesying against Israel, whose destruction is nigh. There is no salvation for her. God's judgment and righteousness are at hand.

But, as always, there are a remnant of believers still in the land. Illustrating this in verse 3, in each of the decimated cities. A remnant because of the promise of the Lord that those who seek Him shall live.

Note that the number is not set in stone, it is an example. The remnant aren't chosen by God, and it isn't a promise that there will be a tenth spared. As with this entire chapter, it is an encouragement to repent towards God.

Many Dispensationalists put the wrong emphasis of there being a remnant on God to elect one. To be a Calvinist God Who forces certain men to be saved. They sometimes argue that verses like this are a guarantee that God has decided to set some people aside to be saved, rather than a process by which they can be. And so, the emphasis should be on the promise, that those who call on His name shall be saved.

Amos, speaking the word of God warns, seek Him, not Bethel in the Northern Kingdom of Israel where a golden calf was set up by King Jeroboam as a false religion. Not in Gilgal, on the Jordan where idolatrous practices to false gods were held. These vain hopes would come to naught.

Seek the Lord and ye shall live!

Failing that, He promises His wrath will consume them.

And they, specifically the children of Joseph, 'all Ephraim" as the prophets call the Northern Kingdom of Israel, deserve it. They turn right judgment to wormwood, thinking it bitter, rejecting the way of righteousness. They rebuke prophets, hating them that preach God's word. They take advantage of the poor and the weak. They build up their riches by their unrighteousness. They afflict the just, take bribes and turn aside the poor seeking help. They show no mercy and so God's mercy is gone from them.

But the offer stands;

*Seek him that maketh the seven stars and Orion, and turneth the shadow of death into the morning, and maketh the day dark with night: that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name: That strengtheneth the spoiled against the strong, so that the spoiled shall come against the fortress.*

Amos preaches against sin and warns of the coming judgment, and the offer of hope in salvation by faith in the Lord. Just as we are called to do today.

teachings.title: Heap coals of fire on his head
teachings.summary: Unlike Jonah, believers must show mercy to enemies, including giving them the bread of life and water of the gospel, remembering the mercy God showed them.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 5:44-45**
*But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.*

**Romans 9:15-16**
*For he saith to Moses, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion. So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy.*

**Proverbs 25:21-23**
*If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord shall reward thee. The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.*

Perhaps the hardest thing in the Christian life, showing mercy to those who hate us and whom we hate. But if God chooses us to be a blessing to another, it isn't on us to question why. We shouldn't be as Jonah.

And if they are hardened against us, that's on them. Our mercy will be as hot coals upon their head.

**Romans 12:20**
*Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.*

Note the spiritual application of this. Your enemy hungers and thirsts. For what? Food and water? Or truth and the repentance unto faith in Christ?

Will the coals of fire make them angrier and dug in against you? Or remind them of the Hell that awaits them?

Will you withhold that bread that came down from Heaven? The waters of life that you've drank?

Are there many who don't know their right hand from left?

Only God knows.

Remember the mercy God showed you, and let that be what guides your spirit. Don't be as Jonah, and let your anger consume you.

teachings.title: Take with you words: Hosea's sinner's prayer
teachings.summary: Hosea's final appeal is a sinner's prayer: by confessing with our mouths we receive the free gift of eternal life, not by idols or our own works, and God heals our backsliding.
teachings.text:
Here, in the final chapter of **Hosea**, the Lord speaks through the prophet to make one final appeal of the gospel, that whosoever believes be saved.

He calls for Israel to repentance towards God, that they have fallen in their sin. (For all have fallen short)

*Take with you words, and turn to the Lord: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive us graciously*, this is a sinner's prayer. (That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth...)

We are offered the free gift of eternal life in Christ, by the promise of a gracious God, Who takes away our sins, by the confession of our mouths. By the calves, the sin offering of our lips. Giving thanks to His name.

False gods shall not save us, nor the works of our hands. Note the double meaning here, both idols and literally the trust in our own works. For the Lord God is Father to the fatherless, in His mercy.

He heals our backsliding, loves us freely. We are no longer appointed to His wrath.

The Lord promises we will be watered as the lilies of the field. Taking root, spreading out like an olive tree. Growing as the vine.

And Ephraim, all Israel, will bring forth His fruit. After their kind.

*Who is wise, and he shall understand these things? prudent, and he shall know them? for the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them: but the transgressors shall fall therein.*

He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

teachings.title: Turn again unto the Lord, the remnant
teachings.summary: Hezekiah preached to Israel's remnant that God's wrath could still be turned away, and 2 Chronicles 7:14 is a standing promise, so even in a wicked nation we compel men to return to the Lord.
teachings.text:
*Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria. And be not ye like your fathers, and like your brethren, which trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, who therefore gave them up to desolation, as ye see. Now be ye not stiffnecked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves unto the Lord, and enter into his sanctuary, which he hath sanctified for ever: and serve the Lord your God, that the fierceness of his wrath may turn away from you. For if ye turn again unto the Lord, your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that lead them captive, so that they shall come again into this land: for the Lord your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him.*

Hezekiah is preaching the word of God to the lost sheep of Israel. The Northern Kingdom had been made nearly desolate by the Assyrians. A remnant still remained, and Ephraim and Manasseh were yet to be wiped out. There was still time and hope for them as a nation of people who called themselves after His name. The fierceness of His wrath could still be turned away.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

This is a standing promise to Christians, from a God who cannot lie. God, who is longsuffering and merciful, Who rewards those who diligently seek him. Who runs to meet the prodigals coming home to Him.

Very apt timing, the day before our elections here in the United States. Not that a godly person is on the ballot. Not that our wicked nation deserves healing.

But as bad as the people are, and as unclean, we are to compel them to come. To turn back to the Lord, that the fierceness of His wrath be delayed, that a remnant will hear and believe, and His children will get right and sanctify themselves, so that He may forgive us our sin and heal our land.

teachings.title: Why Christ died in this manner
teachings.summary: Every sacrifice from Adam onward pictured the Lamb slain, and the cross and resurrection had to happen before witnesses so that all nations could hear the gospel and believe without seeing.
teachings.text:
I recently was giving the gospel to someone who said, "I understand God loves us, and that His Son, Jesus was born and died and rose again for us, but I struggle with the question; Why?" Not as in why did God do this, which we know is because He so loved us. But why in this manner?

I think one of the reasons is that man by our nature we know sin requires a sacrifice for atonement.

Of course every animal sacrificed from Adam and Eve and God showing them the way, through righteous Abel, to Noah disembarking from the ark, to Abraham with Melchizedek, to Moses and Arron and the Levitical priests, were pictures given by God of the actual sacrifice to come. The Lamb slain before the foundation of the world. And they who trusted in the Christ to come were saved by that faith. But without some means of understanding, it was difficult for them to form faith. Thus the process laid out in the law.

But for the other nations called, after the crucifixion and resurrection, the one sacrifice made for all time, for all sin, by Jesus' blood, man needed to understand it clearly. And so we place trust in His word. Faith being the evidence of things not seen, which comes from hearing His word. There needed to be witnesses. It had to happen here, in this world that others would believe, sight unseen.

As Jesus says to Thomas, *blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.*

Without the prophets and scriptures promising Christ, the sacrifice of Christ, and without the witnesses to the resurrection testifying of Christ, I think man would not believe God wanted to forgive them. Without the gospel preached, a witness, exactly as it stands:

**1 Corinthians 15:1-8**
*Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye have received, and wherein ye stand; By which also ye are saved, if ye keep in memory what I preached unto you, unless ye have believed in vain. For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures: And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep. After that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles. And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.*

teachings.title: Matthew 23 and the Catholic catechism
teachings.summary: Reads Jesus' woes on the scribes and Pharisees as describing Catholic and related false religion, noting that their dogmas keep people from believing the gospel.
teachings.text:
It's the most wicked of all their damnable heresies and doctrines of devils.

Calling faith "sin."

*For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men's shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.

But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.

Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.*

In **Matthew 23**, as Jesus preaches hard against the Jewish religious leaders who perverted the law and led their charges to perdition, He points out their pride in their fathers and their tradition, despite their fathers being the same that killed the prophets of God:

*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because** ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.**

Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, **that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets.***

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers**.

**Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?**

Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.*

A scathing indictment of the Jews, and the unbelieving Israelites that came before them, but it is also damning the Roman Catholic Church that came after, and those that swear by its "fathers" today.

Those who build up the tombs of the martyrs, the early saints whom the apostate church murdered by the millions. Who now change history and claim a false succession, robbing Peter, betraying Paul.

Jesus sent among them prophets and holy men and scribes, those made righteous by faith, not by denomination and sacraments and rites, and they crucified them and burned them at the stake, flayed them and put whole churches to the sword. Often burning copies of God's word on the same pyre as the people found with them.

They claim a lineage with men who persecuted the faithful from city to city, who slew the elect for a millennium, and then the harlot daughters of that protested their whore mother picked up where she left off, and slew Christians all the more.

***Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers.***

Embrace your tradition. Vipers. Hypocrites. Serpents.

***How can ye escape the damnation of hell?***

If you read the chapter and picture each verse, and how it applies to the Roman Catholic Church and the schisms off of it, you understand that this is as prophetic as chapter 24.

And Paul, Peter and Jude all preached on it in scripture. What was and what was to come. And Jesus revealed to John the same vision of the whore. The clouds without water. The wolves in sheep's clothing. It's about Cathodoxy and, new Evangelicals and reformed protestantism. They all fit. False religion is all a sideways corruption of what the Bible says.

And they all have dogmas and heresies that if you sincerely believe them, you won't believe the gospel. There are boxes that you have to consciously check to believe in. Not that they cannot repent to the truth, but some can't.

It's why so many are immune to argument, especially from scripture. They can't be shown because their eyes are blind and they can't hear because they are dull of hearing.

The catechism is a reprobation machine.

Win souls while they are available to win.

teachings.title: You can know you have eternal life
teachings.summary: Sets Romans 3 beside a gospel message for anyone hoping to be good enough for Heaven, offering eternal life as a free gift through faith in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Romans 3:10-20**
*as it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one: There is none that understandeth, There is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; There is none that doeth good, no, not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre; With their tongues they have used deceit; The poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: Their feet are swift to shed blood: Destruction and misery are in their ways: And the way of peace have they not known: There is no fear of God before their eyes. Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law: that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God. Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

teachings.title: Tearing down his father's altar
teachings.summary: Saved believers surrounded by false religion, even family, should stand for the Lord like Gideon, since faithful obedience convinces others more than words.
teachings.text:
Gideon, the son of Joash, from the Abiezrite clan, was of the tribe of Manasseh, living in Ophrah, which is on the promised land side of the Jordan, where the western half tribe of Manasseh resided. The Midianites, on the eastern side of the Jordan south of Edom and Moab. This is how extensive the reach of the Midianites were, as they rated Israel to take as spoil everything they planted. God sent them against Israel for their falling away and worship of Baal.

And to drive home the point of how extensive that abomination was, We see that all of the people living in Ophrah including his own father, worshiped at an altar and a grove dedicated to the Canaanite god.

Gideon was clearly a believer in the Lord, though he questioned why they suffered so. But he knew why, He was surrounded by it. It was punishment for their adultery.

Today many Christians, especially those of us who may have gotten saved from a Bible way to heaven video, or through talking to people online, or by a door-knocker on a missions trip or soul-winning marathon. They believe in the Lord and call upon Jesus name and are saved, yet they are surrounded by people who believe in a false god. It can be very difficult in those situations to stand up for the Lord against the popular opinion of those around us. Including our families. It can be hard to do the right thing.

But we see Gideon instructed to tear down the altar and burn the wood of the grove, and he does so. And when the men come inquiring who did it, Gideon's active faith in service to the Lord. Reveals the dead idol that they had been worshiping, his wayward father leading his defense.

Often that is all it takes to bring other people to the understanding of the Lord. To just stand up and do the next right thing as He is presented it to you. Our faithful obedience can convince people far more than our words. And often the only hindrance to doing something great for the Lord that brings others around to the truth is our own fear.

teachings.title: Every man shall give as he is able
teachings.summary: Blessed by God, believers give back as they are able in two main ways, winning souls and executing right judgment for the fatherless and widow.
teachings.text:
*Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee.*

What a concisely phrased explanation of the Christian life, and God's expectations for us. He blessed us, His children. He asks in return that we give to Him as we are able, according to those blessings.

The giving isn't required for the blessing. But the blessing asks for the giving. And we know that there are two main ways the Lord asks us to give unto Him; winning souls and right judgment.

What a day when we are bringing in the sheaves! When the fullness of man has come in, and to the Lord is given the increase.

As the parables of the sower, the wise servant, and others told by Jesus, picturing the Kingdom of God and the fruit that we are called to bring forth, after our kind. The winning of souls through the gospel.

And in judgement, knowing; *Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted.*

It's no coincidence that the reminder of keeping the feasts, bringing the gifts, remembering the blessings given by the Lord to us, is followed immediately by;

*Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.*

That we are to be unspotted, blameless in our judgement. Not being a respecter of persons. Not showing favor to one over another, but executing right judgment. Not taking bribes, which would pervert out judgment. That we be just in our ways that we may live.

The two things we are separated unto God's ministry in the Gospel to do, linked forever in the feasts that are Christ's.

teachings.title: The Ethiopian eunuch: a textbook salvation
teachings.summary: Reads the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8 as salvation by hearing the word and believing Jesus is the risen Christ, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
It still stuns me that there are people who read the story of the Ethiopian eunuch, a textbook salvation; from hearing the word of God from a saved believer, to accepting that Jesus was that promised Christ, who takes away the sins of the world. And then getting baptized, already saved, as a believer, and add things to it of their own.

It's God's word, His testament, that saves. Accepting His word as true. That Jesus is the Risen Christ, and by His blood we are saved. Just as He promised. Plus or minus nothing.

teachings.title: People rediscovering the reprobate doctrine
teachings.summary: Says that as God's wrath is seen on those who reject Him, it opens people to hear the gospel, with Romans 1:16-32 as the text.
teachings.text:
People are rediscovering the Reprobate Doctrine on their own. God's wrath, revealed from Heaven against those who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge. Who are past feeling. Conscience seared as with a hot iron.

It's a great time to preach the Gospel to those noticing

People, on their own observations, are being shown by God's wrath the truth of His glory, and it opens them up to receive from us the Gospel of grace and mercy. It is part of God's purpose that people be led to Christ by the fall of others who reject Him.

**Romans 1:16-32**
*For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek. For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Provoke to emulation and save some
teachings.summary: Paul's wish is that by provoking his kinsmen to jealousy he might save some, conditions that dispensationalists twist into will and all.
teachings.text:
So consider this context as we read the next verse;

*Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles; how much more their fulness?*

Paul says he is speaking to the Gentiles here. Asking them a question as the apostle to them; if the world is made rich in Christ because the unregenerate Jews fell, can you imagine how much more the glory of God would be revealed by their coming to believe?

Recall that Paul's still talking about his own wish, that his brethren after the flesh be saved. He has already concluded that only a remnant are, and that blindness has come on the rest. That only by being part of the election of grace, given to believers, that they can be saved and made heirs in Christ. God is not a respecter of persons. There is no Jew or Greek in Christ.

In that context, we can see Paul's wish for them expressed by the rhetorical question he asks the reader; if their fall was to bring salvation to the world, how much greater would it be if the salvation of the world brought them back?

*If by any means I may provoke to emulation then which are of my flesh, and might save some of them.*

This is the point of the jealousy God hopes to provoke in them. That some might be saved.

If...may...might...some.

Many dispensationalists will twist this series of conditions to mean "will" and "all."

teachings.title: Peace, peace, when there is no peace
teachings.summary: False prophets preach peace, prosperity and a pre-tribulation escape to itching ears, but true preachers warn of judgment and call men to repent and find peace only in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 6:13-15**
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

False prophets, claiming to speak the words of God, come with soothing words of peace. Peace with God, despite the sins of the people. Peace with the land, despite the blood of innocents. Peace with those who practice Idolatry and wickedness, in ecumenicalism.

They preach prosperity and health to people with itching ears.

**2 Timothy 4:3-4**
*For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.*

Today, many false prophets also claim that believers won't see tribulation, but rather will be spared destruction, raptured before it begins.

But what does Jeremiah say to Hannah? *The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.*

Prophets who come with the word of God preach destruction and repentance.

And, in like manner, today we have the word of God, and we are called to do the same.

**Jude 1:22-23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: and others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

We preach the acceptable year of the Lord. That judgment is coming to every man, and Hell with it. To repent towards God and faith in His Son for deliverance. That man cannot know peace except in Christ. These are the word of God given us in scripture with the command to love one another, to set at liberty from the bonds of the law. To reconcile man with God before it's too late.

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: We have no excuse
teachings.summary: Since we do not face death for preaching as the prophets did, we have no excuse not to serve, and should rejoice in tribulation.
teachings.text:
Be thankful for living when we do, in times where we aren't directly threatened with stocks, stripes or death for the preaching of the cross. We have no excuse.

We live in a time and place where, while we may see tribulation, where we may have the god of this world come against us if we strive for the Gospel, doing our Father's will. Winning souls. Edifying the brethren. We won't face death the way the prophets did. Praise God.

And so we have no excuse.

In fact, if you have done anything for the Lord, you may have already felt the attacks of Satan and his children on you. And yet, if you rejoice in the temptations and praise God for the tribulation that worketh patience in you, you will be delivered.

We have no excuse.

And if the times become more hostile, and persecution for the faith more common, still rejoice.

**Matthew 10:28**
*And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell*.

We will still have no excuse.

teachings.title: The clearest presentation of the gospel in John 3
teachings.summary: Reads John 3 as the clearest gospel from Jesus: all are condemned by sin, and whosoever believes on the Son has everlasting life, with nothing added.
teachings.text:
**John 3***
14 And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:

15 That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

16 For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

17 For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

18 He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
...
33 He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true.

34 For he whom God hath sent speaketh the words of God: for God giveth not the Spirit by measure unto him.

35 The Father loveth the Son, and hath given all things into his hand.

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
*.

This is the clearest presentation of the Gospel of God, given by Jesus and note all the elements contained in it. That we are condemned by sin. But God so loved the world, that's everyone in it, that whosoever shall believe, that is trust and have faith in Christ Jesus, not our works or our genealogy or our ability to turn from sin, but faith alone, has eternal life and shall not perish.

This is what we believe to be saved.

If you don't accept any element of this or add something to it, you deny the record and aren't saved. You are perishing.

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: What must I do to be saved
teachings.summary: Answering a seeker with repent of your sins instead of believe on the Lord Jesus Christ only leads to confusion, discouragement and perdition.
teachings.text:
And imagine being an unsaved but seeking person, desperate to know what they must do to be saved, like the Philippian jailer, and you ask "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

And the answer isn't "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ," but instead is "well, you have to repent of your sins."

"What does that mean? Like stop sinning? What if I can't? Which sins? The really bad ones? What if I don't realize it's a sin? What if I slip up?"

"Well, try to avoid sin. You have to want to avoid sin."

"How? I can't be saved if I don't try to avoid sin? I already am trying not to drink/smoke/watch porn. Is that good enough? How will I know if it's good enough? If I'm good enough?"

"Well then make Jesus your boss. Make him the Lord of your life."

"Isn't He already? What does that even mean? Do I have to sell everything and follow Him like the young rich man?"

Etc...
